tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

```json
  },
  "round_limit": 10,

```

### 0.2 Top-level fields: what to expect, what uses it

| Field | Expect | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `case_id`, `set` | `case:P01`…`P19` (practice), `case:D01`/`D02` (sandbox), hidden IDs in `final` | cache keys (R13.17), logs |
| `hosted` | practice only; `true` on the 10 playable cases (P01-P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18) | - |
| `type` | `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` | `TYPE_LEVERS` (R1.5), case questions (R9.4), anchor (R4.1, R13.12) |
| `title`, `briefing` | prose; repeats need, goal, need lead time, fallback and must-haves in words. The structured `buyer` block is the source of truth - never parse numbers from the briefing | profile prompt (R1.3), writer context (R9.2) |
| `trigger_doc` | a `doc:` ID (the supplier's letter / RFQ document) | data arguments - notice vs contract (R13.9) |
| `parts` | 1 part, except bundling (P07: 4, P15: 3) - still **one** `unit_price` per sheet | dossier (R1.1), should-cost (R2.1) |
| `suppliers` | 1 supplier; 2-3 = an RFQ (P05: 3, P06: 2; sandbox D02: 2) | RFQ handling (sections 8, 12.6) |
| `negotiable` | always contains `unit_price`, plus 2-3 of the fields below. A term sheet must carry **exactly** these fields or it is a `422` | sheets (R6, R11.11), lever table (R12.3) |
| `fixed_terms` | the case's other fields with their values (fields named in neither list - e.g. `ppm_commitment` outside quality cases - take the supplier's standard terms) | C computation, `describe` (R13.14) |
| `term_options` | allowed values per negotiable field except `unit_price` - send nothing else | lever table (R12.3), steps (R13.1), repair (R11.9) |
| `round_limit` | 10 in every case so far - read it, do not assume it | horizon H (R5.1), close rules (R7.5-R7.6) |
| `refs` | 3-5 starting IDs (`doc`, `ctr`, `sc`, `quote`); "a start, not the whole story" | dossier (R1.1), arguments (R9.5) |
| `facts` | **hidden cases only**: case-specific facts in `facts.json` format, citable in that case | merge into the claim data before computing arguments (R13.9) |
| `wave`, `theme`, `open`, `seconds_left` | **final only**; `seconds_left` until the 8-minute wave cap | case clock (R11.14-R11.16) - read `seconds_left`, don't assume 480 |

### 0.3 Negotiable fields and their options (all practice cases)

| Field | Options seen | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_price` | free, EUR with 2 decimals | the only free field |
| `payment_days` | always `[14, 30, 45, 60, 90]` | reference is 60; fixed at 30-60 where not negotiable |
| `contract_months` | always `[12, 24, 36]` | with `horizon_years` = 2, 12 months leaves half the need uncovered (R12.2) |
| `volume_per_year` | three steps around the need, e.g. `[16379, 19890, 23400]` (≈ 70 / 85 / 100 % or 80 / 100 / 120 %) | where fixed it equals `need_per_year` |
| `effective_date` | `["2026-11-01", "2027-01-01", "2027-04-01"]` (price_increase) | the horizon starts at the earliest option; later = more units at `current_unit_price` |
| `lead_time_days` | 3-5 values, e.g. `[28, 35, 42, 56]` | compare with `need_lead_time_days`; often a must-have |
| `index_clause` | `null` + one series at deadband 0 / 3 / 5 %, fixed `material_share` (0.2-0.8) and `base_month` `"2026-08"` | the clause object must match an option exactly |
| `ppm_commitment` | `[300, 800, 1500, 2500]` (quality) | priced with `cost_per_defect` and the chargeback |
| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | `[0, 150, 300, 500]` (quality) | capped at `cost_per_defect` in C |
| `tooling_eur` | `[0, 7500, 15000]` (P06) | one-off, added to C |
| `incoterm` | `EXW` / `FCA` / `DAP`; fixed in every practice case | freight from `freight_eur_per_unit`; DAP is always 0.0 |

### 0.4 The `buyer` block: what to expect

| Field | Range seen | Pattern to rely on |
|---|---|---|
| `need_per_year` | 3,420 - 94,800 | units; with `horizon_years` the total need = N × H |
| `horizon_years` | `1` / `1.0` or `2` / `2.0` (API allows ≤ 3) | int **or** float - normalise; 1-year cases have `contract_months` fixed at 12 |
| `current_unit_price` | 4.20 - 412.74 | equals the fallback price in an RFQ (new part) |
| `fallback_unit_price` | 1.00 - 1.25 × current | 1.25 × in the capacity cases: walking is expensive |
| `interest_rate` | always 0.08 | our cost of money (R2.2) |
| `reference_payment_days` | always 60 | paying earlier than 60 days costs us interest |
| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | 5-59 days; EUR 40-2,400/day | capacity cases carry the high late cost |
| `cost_per_defect` | 0 - 780 | 0 in raw_material cases: ppm is worthless there |
| `category_goal` | `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage`, `routine` | selects the playbook row (R13.10) and the anchor cut (R4.1) |
| `fallback_risk_pct` | follows the goal: leverage 3, routine 5, quality_first 8, stabilise 10, secure_supply 25 | uncovered need is the costliest mistake in secure_supply |
| `index_risk_pct` | follows the goal: leverage 1, routine / quality_first 2, secure_supply 3, stabilise 4 | a clause costs us this share of indexed spend on top of the path |
| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | 0.5-10 %; EUR 5,000-31,920 per point-year - **only** for stabilise and secure_supply, `null` otherwise | the margin charge (R2.3, R13.8); treat `null` as "no charge" |
| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}`, DAP always 0.0 | per committed unit |
| `index_paths` | `{}` or one series: `AS-14404` +0.06, `CU-NOTATION` +0.05, `PPI-C241` +0.03 | the expected move of the clause's series; a series missing here has path 0 |
| `must_haves` | `[]` or one rule: `lead_time_days <= 42` (P05, P09), `<= 84` (P06), `volume_per_year >= 22230` (P10), `ppm_commitment <= 1500` (P11) | a deal that breaks one scores **0** - check every sheet and every accept against them (R6.7, R11.9) |
| `alternative` | `kind` = `quote` (`ref` = `quote:72000NN`, full `terms`), `current_contract` (`ref` = a `ctr:` ID **or `null`**, full `terms`), or `none` (`ref` null, `terms` `{}`) | C_alt = C(alternative terms); with `none`, no deal = uncovered need at the fallback price, score 0 |

### 0.5 Case types as they appear

| Type | Goals seen | Negotiable besides price | Typical must-have / alternative |
|---|---|---|---|
| `price_increase` | stabilise, leverage | effective_date, payment_days, index_clause or volume | quote or none |
| `renewal` | stabilise, routine | payment_days, contract_months, volume, index_clause | quote or none; H = 2 |
| `rfq` | leverage, stabilise | payment_days, lead_time_days, tooling_eur | lead-time must-have; `alternative: none` |
| `bundling` | routine | payment_days, contract_months | `current_contract`; 3-4 parts, one price |
| `raw_material` | leverage | index_clause, payment_days, contract_months | quote; `index_paths` set; `cost_per_defect` 0 |
| `capacity` | secure_supply | volume_per_year, lead_time_days, contract_months / payment_days | volume or lead-time must-have; fallback 1.25 × |
| `quality` | quality_first | ppm_commitment, chargeback, (lead_time_days) | ppm must-have or `current_contract` |

A hidden case may combine these differently or bring a new type: take the levers from `negotiable`
when `type` is unknown, and the `routine` playbook row when `category_goal` is unknown.

### 0.6 The opening quotes and the replies

`POST /v1/sessions` also returns `opening`, one entry per supplier:

```json
"sup:70240": {"offer_id": "offer:70240-0", "round": 0, "status": "open",
              "terms": {"unit_price": 31.5, "lead_time_days": 52},
              "alternatives": [],
              "missing_fields": ["payment_days"],
              "claims": [], "claim_results": [],
              "signals": {"reply_delay_days": 4, "validity_days": 30},
              "text": "Hello, Thank you for your enquiry. ..."}
```

- **`terms` can be partial.** Fields in `missing_fields` close on the supplier's **standard terms**
  (in the quote PDF) - fill them from the PDF before computing C; never assume our reference values.
- **An opening quote can break a must-have** (P05: 52 days against `<= 42`) - repair it (R11.9).
- `alternatives`: `[{offer_id, terms}]` - extra packages, acceptable like the main sheet (R12.11).
- Replies (`POST …/messages`) carry `status` (`open`, `final_offer`, `agreed`, `walked_away`,
  `no_bid`), `term_sheets` (its standing offer, `offer:` ID), `claim_results` per argument,
  `signals`, `missing_fields` and `attachments` (cost breakdown XLSX, 8D PDF, delivery schedule).

### 0.7 What to compute from the case JSON before the first message

1. Validate: every `negotiable` field except `unit_price` has `term_options`; no field is both
   fixed and negotiable; must-haves name real fields.
2. C(terms) with `arena_kit.total_cost`, the opening C of every supplier (standard terms filled),
   and C_alt from `buyer.alternative`.
3. Coverage: does `contract_months` × `volume_per_year` cover `need_per_year` × `horizon_years`?
   If an option closes the gap and lowers C, it goes into message 1 (R12.1-R12.2).
4. The lever table (R12.3) over `term_options`, the playbook row for `category_goal` (R13.10), the
   anchor (R4, R13.12) and the floor (R2.1, R6.5).
5. The must-have filter every sheet and every accept passes through.
6. The clock: `round_limit` and, in the final, `seconds_left`.

## Evidence

From `knowledge/sessions.jsonl` on `feature/team-agent` (practice sessions, 10 Oct 2026).

## 1. Prepare before the clock

- **R1.1 Supplier dossier.** Before the session's first move, gather for every supplier everything
  in the data package: call and meeting notes, letters, past negotiations (asked vs settled), its
  financials, our payment record, scorecards, should-cost, the part's cost drivers and contract
  clauses (`dossier.gather`, Sunday release included). Cache it per supplier and parts.
- **R1.2 Cash signals.** Scan the dossier for cash-pressure words (cash, liquidity, skonto, prepay,
  credit line, working capital, insolvency, short-time work, "within N days") and record the hits.
- **R1.3 One profile call per supplier, in parallel.** A model reads the dossier plus the computed
  data arguments and returns JSON only:
  `persona, tone, pressures[], wants[], levers[], avoid[], cash_short, claim_ranking[], questions[], angle`.
  Timeout 90 s for all profiles together.
- **R1.4 Validate the profile.** `levers` are mapped onto the case's negotiable field names and
  `claim_ranking` onto real argument keys; anything that does not match is dropped. `cash_short` is
  true if the model says so, or if the dossier has cash signals and payment_days is the top lever.
- **R1.5 Default profile.** If the call fails or times out, use a default profile: polite, factual,
  constructive tone; levers = payment_days first when cash signals exist, then the case type's levers
  (`TYPE_LEVERS` below). A missing profile never costs the case.

`TYPE_LEVERS`: price_increase → effective_date, payment_days · raw_material → index_clause,
payment_days, contract_months · renewal → contract_months, volume_per_year, payment_days · bundling →
contract_months, payment_days · capacity → volume_per_year, lead_time_days, contract_months ·
quality → chargeback_eur_per_complaint, ppm_commitment · rfq → payment_days, lead_time_days, tooling_eur.

## 2. Our estimate of the supplier

- **R2.1 Full cost, calibrated.** In this order: the supplier's own cost-breakdown XLSX (sum of EUR
  elements, without margin and totals); else should-cost / 1.02 (fits the arena's relationship charge
  over 31 recorded deals - `FULL_COST_K` in `team/agent.py` and the current MESO agent); else opening
  price / 1.10. Not too high: a high floor made BuyerAgent stop pushing (P01, 10 Oct: accepted 136.30
  where 133.70 was reachable). Not too low either: with its "low end of the confidence band"
  estimate BuyerAgent saw no cost in squeezing P02's supplier to EUR 351 - the arena charged EUR
  124,110 for it (score 0.211; DualAgent 0.385 at EUR 373).
- **R2.2 Cost of money.** The buyer's interest rate, plus 6 points for a supplier short of cash.
  Once the supplier has priced payment days itself (two of its sheets differ only in payment), use
  that revealed rate instead (slope × 360, clamped to 3-40 %) - see R12.4.
- **R2.3 Margin charge only where the goal has one.** C includes the supplier's margin penalty only
  for stabilise and secure_supply.

## 3. What we negotiate on

- **R3.1 Best sheet on the table.** For each thread, take the supplier's cheapest offer for us among
  its standing sheet *and* its alternatives, preferring ones that keep the must-haves.
- **R3.2 Both-sides-gain structure (`mutual_combo`).** Move each of the supplier's non-price terms
  toward what the supplier prefers for as long as that also lowers our C (e.g. a longer contract that
  covers our whole need). The price is negotiated on this structure, not on the quote as sent.
- **R3.3 Asks are never free (`reference_combo`).** Terms the supplier pulled beyond our reference
  (payment days, volume, contract length, lead time, no index clause) are put back where that saves
  us money before pricing the target - what it asks for is paid for in price.

## 4. The opening anchor

- **R4.1 Anchor from the data.** The lowest of: the goal's cut off the best quote (leverage 12 %,
  routine 8 %, quality_first 6 %, stabilise 6 %, secure_supply 5 %); the current price (no increase
  at all) for price_increase and raw_material cases; the fair price = should-cost / (1 − margin)
  (leverage 5 %, routine 6 %, quality_first 8 %; the sustainable margin for relationship goals).
- **R4.2 Credibility limits.** Never more than 25 % under the supplier's price; never under its
  estimated full cost × 1.01; never under the price at which C stops falling.
- **R4.3 RFQ.** Every bidder is anchored to the best quote in the case, not its own (D02: anchored
  to its own 17.10, the dearer bidder agreed to 15.09 at once; about 13 was reachable).
- **R4.4 Fixed anchor.** The anchor is set once per thread.

## 5. Concessions: reciprocal, never stuck

- **R5.1 Curve.** Our k-th offer closes `1 − (1 − k/H)^1.6` of the gap from the anchor to the
  supplier's C; H = 6 (5 in an RFQ). Steps shrink over time.
- **R5.2 Reciprocity.** Track the supplier's C after every reply (one entry per reply, so a hold shows
  as a zero step). If it moved more than 0.1 % of C: our step = max(min(planned, 0.5 × its step),
  0.4 % of C). We move by less than it did, but always visibly.
- **R5.3 Deadlock breaker (the key difference from DualAgent).** If the supplier did not move, hold
  **once**; the next round make one real step to break the deadlock: at least 15 % of the C gap left
  (TeamAgent's measure, R12.5), and never less than 0.4 % of C. Never stall two rounds, never close
  just because both sides held. Never a token step (D01: "a nominal adjustment of one cent" was
  called out).
- **R5.4 Still moving means ask again.** If the supplier's offer meets our target but it is still
  conceding (> 0.4 % of C last round) and more than 3 rounds are left, set the target to
  `their C − 0.5 × their last step` and keep negotiating.
- **R5.5 Caps.** The target never exceeds 0.995 × the alternative's C. In an RFQ it is at most 0.99 ×
  the best rival's C, and never below the anchor.

## 6. Term sheets

- **R6.1 Up to three sheets, all at the target C** (`strategy.sheets`): our terms (every term at its
  best for us, at a higher price), their terms (the both-sides-gain structure), and a give (one lever
  from the profile moved toward the supplier, for a lower price). "Our terms" goes first.
- **R6.2 Shared surplus on a give.** When a term is worth more to the supplier than it costs us (e.g.
  faster payment to a cash-short supplier), price the give halfway between our equal-cost price and the
  supplier's indifference price (`give_price`, `SURPLUS_SHARE = 0.5`). Both sides are better off
  taking it.
- **R6.3 The supplier asked for something.** Send two sheets instead: exactly its ask at a lower
  price (shared surplus), and our reference terms at the target price. No third sheet that blurs the
  trade (`ask_sheets`).
- **R6.4 Decoy.** Arrange the sheets as lean / recommended / other. The lean one is the recommended
  sheet 2 % cheaper with the supplier's most-valued term moved our way, so the middle one looks
  sensible. It is safe: if the supplier takes the lean one, that is better for us (`with_decoy`).
- **R6.5 Sheet floor.** No sheet below max(estimated full cost × 0.97, 75 % of the supplier's price).
  P18, 10 Oct: a give at 28 % under was not credible and the supplier did not move.
- **R6.6 Out of reach.** If no sheet fits the target, send the supplier's own terms at
  max(floor, 99 % of its price), provided the must-haves hold.
- **R6.7 Every sheet keeps the must-haves** and is cheaper than what the supplier asks.

## 7. When to close

Accept the cheapest standing sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats the alternative when:

- **R7.1** the supplier agreed to our terms;
- **R7.2** it made a final offer (single thread; in an RFQ only if every thread is final or this is
  the best offer on the table);
- **R7.3** its offer meets our next target - unless it is still moving with more than 3 rounds left
  (R5.4);
- **R7.4** its offer is as good as what we last offered;
- **R7.5** at most one round is left in the thread (or in every RFQ thread);
- **R7.6** the planned rounds are over (H + 2 offers in every thread).

Walk away only when nothing on the table is acceptable and every thread is at a final offer or out of
rounds. **No** deadlock close and **no** walk-risk close: those ended DualAgent's P11 and P18 early.

## 8. RFQ handling

- **R8.1** Plan every live thread each round and write all their e-mails in parallel, so no thread
  idles into the 60-second rule.
- **R8.2** With more than two live threads, stop answering bidders more than 25 % dearer than the
  best once we have sent them two offers.
- **R8.3** Rival prices are cited as checkable arguments (`offer:` IDs), once per supplier.

## 9. The e-mail

- **R9.1 The model writes words only** (the kit's `writing.SYSTEM` JSON parts: salutation, opening,
  argument keys, bridge, question, closing). Code inserts the arguments word for word and the options
  paragraph from the term sheets, then lints (no leaks, no figures that are not in the material, no
  unknown IDs).
- **R9.2 What the writer sees:** the supplier's profile (persona, tone, pressures, wants, avoid,
  angle); its last e-mail with sender, status, subject and non-quote attachments; how our arguments
  have checked out so far; our last two e-mails; how far it moved toward us in % since our last
  e-mail; the options; up to 6 arguments ranked by the profile's `claim_ranking`; the questions.
- **R9.3 Plain stance per move** (`_stance`):
  - first e-mail: "We open: our options are ambitious; give the reasons, not apologies."
  - hold while they are still coming down: acknowledge the step briefly, say the price is still too
    high and why;
  - hold because they did not move: polite but firm, do not thank them for flexibility they did not
    show, give one concrete reason or ask what would let them move;
  - step: "a modest step - this costs us and we expect a step back."
- **R9.4 Questions.** One per e-mail at most, never repeated: a cost breakdown once (unless already
  asked or received - an open supplier sends one, and R2.1 uses it), then the case type's question
  (8D report, delivery schedule, shortest lead time, which cost elements rose, which volume or term
  would improve the price, bundle parts, fair base month and deadband), then the profile's questions.
- **R9.5 Arguments.** From `claims.candidates` (code-computed, checked IDs). Each ID once per case;
  an argument that came back `contradicted` is never used again; news the profile ranks as helpful
  counts as favourable. Even a fallback e-mail carries the two best arguments.
- **R9.6 Company name** from the data, else from the supplier's subject ("Quote from X:") or
  signature - never the bare supplier ID (D02: "Dear colleagues at sup:DEMO-J1").
- **R9.7 Allowed figures** come only from the supplier's e-mails, the trigger letter, the contract
  clauses, our arguments and the options paragraph.

## 10. Robustness and timing

- **R10.1** The writer has 35 s; a late or failed call is replaced by a code-written plain e-mail
  with the same sheets and arguments.
- **R10.2** A planni

# SpecAgent design decisions

The implementation follows `NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md`. This file collects choices previously
recorded only in docstrings and records how requirements that overlap are reconciled.
Code controls prices, term sheets, accept/walk decisions, claims and deadlines. The model profiles
suppliers, extracts what they said and writes the surrounding email text. Every model call has a
deadline and a code fallback.

## Rule precedence

| Overlap | Decision and reason |
|---|---|
| R4.1 vs R13.10 anchors | Use the deeper cut: leverage 15%, routine 10%, quality 8%, stabilise 6%, secure supply 5%; RFQs add 4 points. Apply the current-price/fair-price candidates and credibility limits afterwards. The relationship cost minimum is a floor, rather than an independent second anchor. |
| R5.2 reciprocity vs R12.5 15% steps | The 15% gap rule determines the planned step; reciprocity caps it when the supplier moved less. The 0.4% visible-step minimum wins over that cap, as R5.2 explicitly specifies. A nonmoving supplier gets one hold, then a real step. |
| R5.4 vs no retreat | Continue negotiating while a supplier is still moving, but do not ask below our previous target merely because the supplier improved. Supplier and alternative caps can still lower the target. |
| R6 menus vs R13.1 sequential terms | After coverage, heavy terms use a single-term equal-cost menu. Price rounds use the reference/give/decoy menu. A supplier ask may replace that menu with two clear trade packages. |
| R13.1 goal order vs R12.7 payment probe | A payment term worth stepping goes first, so the first menu also reveals payment preference. Remaining terms follow goal priority, then EUR weight; at most three terms. |
| R13.3 reopen vs R13.4 choice | A costly term gets at most one reopen. A menu with fewer than two credible packages is skipped and never recorded as a step or a lock. Its best value stays available in price rounds. |
| R13.5 revealed price vs an earlier menu lock | A supplier's own differently priced alternative overrides the earlier menu pick when its actual package costs us less. Persist that revealed value across replies without alternatives. Compare numeric terms by value, so `0` and `0.0` are the same lock. |
| R12.8 deadband vs R13.5 actual prices | New demanded-index menus use the supplier's own series and the cheapest deadband at equal unit price. Later supplier-priced alternatives are compared at their actual package costs; a cheaper zero-deadband package can win that revealed-price comparison. This can lose versus negotiating a wider band, and must be measured rather than assumed beneficial. |
| R12.12 final offer vs continued steps | A valid final offer closes at once. Only an unacceptable final gets one repair at its own price. Tone, walk risk and deadlock are never independent close rules. |
| R12.16 wait for rivals vs R13.16 60 seconds | Wait only until 45 seconds after the chosen supplier's reply, leaving 15 seconds to accept. A slow POST is polled from the thread after 3 seconds; waiting 70 seconds could itself exceed the reply clock. |
| R11.14 vs R11.15 clock | No new counter after 360 seconds, and no counter earlier if its estimated round cannot finish by 420. Writer time is also capped by that remaining round budget. Clock starts immediately after session open, before document reading/preparation. A shorter wave moves both marks earlier; zero seconds forces a close. |

## Cost estimates and prices

Supplier full cost comes from its breakdown, otherwise should-cost / 1.02, otherwise opening / 1.10.
For an RFQ whose bids are below should-cost, the lowest opening bid replaces stale should-cost as
the fallback estimate. Later concessions cannot disable the margin penalty: market calibration uses
opening bids, not the lowest price reached during negotiation. Only stabilise and secure-supply
goals include the supplier margin penalty.
The inherited implementation trusts only breakdown/should-cost estimates for the full-cost anchor
and credibility floor. With an opening-price-only estimate it uses the 75%-of-quote floor instead.
This is an additional deviation from literal R4.2/R6.5, which do not exempt an opening estimate;
retained as an explicit tuning decision, not silently described as full compliance.

A missing alternative (`kind: none`) leaves the accept ceiling infinite. A real alternative is
priced with its actual terms. Offers must beat it both with the estimated supplier penalty and
without it. Coverage is requested when it lowers cost; subsequent packages cannot reduce committed
coverage. Coverage repair can explicitly restore the full horizon and annual need.

search for the cost minimum and bisection above that minimum. Prices must use two decimals, so the
literal R13.8 “within EUR 1” is often mathematically impossible: changing the price by EUR 0.01 on

A package need not have a lower unit price than the supplier's offer: a later effective date or
better payment terms can lower total cost despite a higher price. Credibility floors still apply.

still meets the need and must-haves at equal cost, request that instead. This addresses P05's explicit
overtime premium for 28 days when 35 days is sufficient; genuinely valuable speed is not relaxed.

Practice ranges are warnings, not replacement values: a valid case with an unusual interest rate
must use that rate. Missing/invalid fields receive defensive defaults; every warning is logged.
Unknown case types use their actual negotiable fields; unknown goals use the routine playbook.
When a field is both fixed and negotiable in a malformed case, the negotiable definition wins and
the conflict is logged.

Prose alternatives inherit unchanged terms from the main offer before revealed prices are computed.
They cannot be accepted by an invented offer ID: packages found only in prose are offered back for

analyst must occur in the supplier's text, and nonfinite figures are rejected.

the risk threshold even though its printed claim would say 15.0%.

Targets in the requirements are rounded to three decimals (for example the historical P01 score

distinguish previous bests, current results, and unresolved shortfalls.

seconds. They cannot guarantee a server responds or commits an accept by 420 seconds during a
network outage. Hosted logs must be checked for actual closure times, refusals, timeouts and
contradicted claims; simulator scores validate plumbing, not hosted negotiation quality.

an arena timeout while other negotiations continue. Keep such timeouts visible in the report;
do not count them as a clean timing pass merely because the chosen deal closes promptly.

# SpecAgent completion and review — 11 October 2026

The missing test coverage, design notes, sandbox games, local simulator games and hosted practice
evaluation have been completed. This is **not a full acceptance pass**: only P02, P04 and P11 meet
their rounded score targets, and a deliberately idled P05 bidder incurred a timeout. The remaining
performance gaps and explicit requirement deviations are recorded below, not hidden by the successful
deals or by the team's historical leaderboard bests.

## Verification

Final source: **204 tests passed, 1 skipped**, `ruff check arena_kit tests` clean, `git diff --check`
clean. The skipped test is the separately opted-in hosted smoke test for NaiveAgent/LLMAgent
(`ARENA_TEST_URL`/`ARENA_TEST_KEY`); SpecAgent's requested hosted games actually ran, with the
configured OpenAI `gpt-6-astra` model and the user's explicit permission.

| Requirement | Regression coverage |
|---|---|
| R11.2, R11.8, R11.12 | `tests/test_spec_analyst.py`: grounded extraction, decimal/sign boundaries, dates, nonfinite numbers, inherited prose lock-in, tactic eligibility |
| R11.14–R11.15, R12.17 | `tests/test_spec_clock.py`, `tests/test_spec_analyst.py`: virtual clocks, measured rounds, short/zero waves, early close, writer budget/fallback |
| R12.4, R12.14 | `tests/test_spec_steps.py`: inherited revealed slopes, costly lever exclusion, first RFQ rival citation without model waiting |
| R13.1–R13.7 | `tests/test_spec_steps.py`: one-term menus, ranking, option order, one reopen, real two-package choices after guards, persistent/overriding revealed locks, EN/DE alternatives, no identical resend |
| R13.9, R13.11, R13.15 | `tests/test_spec_claims_email.py`: index windows/rounding, rising-index eligibility, notice/ledger, case-only facts, exact volatility threshold, lint and real salutations |
| R13.16 | `tests/test_spec_clock.py`, `tests/test_spec_runner.py`: bounded rival wait, slow-POST polling, refused-accept refresh/retry, full local API games |
| Evaluation accuracy | `tests/test_spec_evaluate.py`: structured timeouts are detected even without timeout wording |

Existing pricing, coverage, sheet guard, close-rule and recorded-negotiation tests were rerun too.
Additional tests cover cost-neutral normal lead times and numeric equality of locked terms (`0` vs
`0.0`).

## Games and score table

D01 and D02 were played with the configured model: scores **0.786949** and **0.649788**, valid deals,
closed after **138.1** and **200.8** seconds from open. Evidence:
[D01](runs/spec-sandbox-d01/D01.json), [D02](runs/spec-sandbox-d02/D02.json).

All three clock-enabled local simulator cases also ended in valid deals: S01 **0.173886**, S02
**0.171836**, S03 **0.633926**. The final-source model repeat is in
[spec-sim-verified](runs/spec-sim-verified/summary.md). An initial simulator setup omitted the data
facts and produced contradicted IDs; the evaluator was corrected to supply the facts and the games
were repeated cleanly. Simulator scores test plumbing, not hosted negotiation quality.

The hosted model sweep is one complete ten-case run. The code-only column is a separate final-source
fallback benchmark, not a claim that model and non-model negotiations are interchangeable. Targets
are compared at three decimals because the requirements round historical raw scores.
The main model sweep preceded the last lead-time/volatility edits; the affected P05 negotiation was
retested with the lead-time fix, followed by a final-source model simulator repeat and a full
final-source code-only hosted sweep. Source fingerprints preserve these distinctions.

| Case | Target | Final code-only | Model sweep | Model seconds from open | Target met |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P01 | 0.941 | 0.827854 | 0.631200 | 113.5 | No |
| P02 | 0.507 | 0.506721 | 0.506721 | 121.3 | Yes, rounded |
| P03 | 0.919 | 0.864105 | 0.864105 | 160.7 | No |
| P04 | 0.860 | 0.860445 | 0.860445 | 118.1 | Yes |
| P05 | 0.781 | 0.676181 | 0.521725 | 170.2 | No |
| P07 | 0.773 | 0.753477 | 0.714517 | 144.9 | No |
| P08 | 0.549 | 0.393752 | 0.332313 | 128.1 | No |
| P10 | 0.671 | 0.662905 | 0.647294 | 34.7 | No |
| P11 | 0.710 | 0.709896 | 0.709896 | 322.0 | Yes, rounded |
| P18 | 0.453 | 0.270425 | 0.319096 | 143.6 | No |

Model sweep mean: **0.610731 (61.07/100)**, versus target mean **0.716400 (71.64/100)**.
Final code-only sweep mean: **0.652576 (65.26/100)**; all ten valid deals, maximum closure time
185.6 seconds, but also one deliberately idled P05 bidder timeout. Fast cached supplier responses
in many repeated code-only games are not a guarantee of real-world latency.
The post-fix, model-backed P05 retest improved to **0.573210**, with 35-day lead time, but remains
below target. Its wall time includes pre-open profiling; closure from open was about 203 seconds.
It is a targeted retest, not a replacement ten-case mean.

Raw scores, threads, sessions, audit records, prompts/replies and source fingerprints:
[model sweep](runs/spec-practice-model/summary.md),
[final code-only sweep](runs/spec-practice-verified/summary.md),
[P05 retest](runs/spec-practice-p05-lead-fix/P05.json).
Earlier experiments are preserved in `runs/spec-practice-code`, `runs/spec-practice-fixed` and
`runs/spec-practice-final`; their intermediate regressions are not represented as successful fixes.

## Below-target investigation and fix outcomes

| Case | Evidence / cause | Fix or measured outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | A lower-total-cost later-date package can need a higher unit price. The original generator rejected it. Model play also locked 30-day payment and a January date after the supplier priced an alternative; its cheaper alternative ID was refused by the arena. | Removed the unit-price ceiling while preserving total-cost/floor guards; enforced real choices after guards and persistent revealed locks. Code play improved from 0.759845 to 0.827854 and obtained April, but at EUR 136.85/30 days rather than historical EUR 135.20/60 days. Model play still missed. |
| P03 | Full coverage is correct. The first credible payment choices at the estimated convex-cost target were 30/45 days; the supplier chose 45 and held EUR 430.09. Historical target play achieved 90 days at EUR 432.29. | Fixed inherited prose slopes and actual-price locks. Repeated code/model games still scored 0.864105. The remaining gap is payment/anchor calibration, not a missing coverage or arithmetic fix. |
| P05 | Quote-PDF defaults carried unnecessary 28-day expedited delivery despite a 35-day need. Suppliers explicitly state that 28 days costs overtime. Dralveck countered at EUR 28, then walked after another low counter; Fuchsreiter became the remaining best deal. | Relax cost-neutral expedited lead times without violating must-haves; bounded accept waiting and skipped model grace on terminal replies. Model score improved 0.521725 → 0.573210. Final code play obtained EUR 29.50/35 days and 0.676181. The anchor/concession path still fails to secure the historical EUR 28.42 deal. |
| P07 | Correct 24-month coverage/90-day payment, but supplier stopped at EUR 5.46 with the model and EUR 5.40 without it, against historical EUR 5.37. | Retested after lock/guard/no-resend fixes. Final offers were accepted promptly, not countered past withdrawal. Further opening/wording calibration remains unproven; no numerical bug was found that explains the residual price gap. |
| P08 | Supplier insisted on an index clause; wider deadband menus incurred a price premium and quickly reached final. Model EUR 5.67/5% band differs from historical EUR 5.47/5% band. | Added demanded-series/deadband filtering and persistent revealed-price locks. Code obtained EUR 5.49/0% band and 0.393752; model scored 0.332313. This policy change did not close the gap and some experiments worsened the score. |
| P10 | Coverage/must-have repair held, but the supplier immediately made a valid final offer: EUR 31.90 with model, EUR 31.70 without, versus historical EUR 31.60. | Verified full 23,400 annual volume/24 months and immediate final acceptance. No unsafe counter after final was used to chase the score. Opening lead-time/price calibration remains a strategy gap. |
| P18 | Payment/index sequencing left EUR 5.60/0% band with model or EUR 5.80/5% band in code play. Cheaper historical/alternative IDs were refused, then the current offer was accepted. | Retested the deadband/lock changes and robust accept ladder. Best observed score in this work was 0.319096, not 0.453; the wider-band experiment regressed. Payment/deadband premium calibration remains unresolved. |

These causes distinguish observed supplier behaviour from inferred tuning opportunities. A passing
unit test does not prove a negotiation will reach a historical score, and cross-run differences do
not establish that model wording alone caused the difference.

## Timing, claims, and consistency review

All ten model cases ended in deals, all returned `must_haves_ok: true`, and all closed before 420
seconds (maximum 322.0). There were **no contradicted claims** and **no buyer emails missing the
Hollerau company signature** in the corrected simulator, sandbox or hosted evidence. Model writer
calls in the ten-case sweep took at most 11.7 seconds, with no writer errors.

The model P05 sweep, its lead-time retest and the final code-only sweep each contain one structured
timeout on the deliberately idled, uncompetitive Hrvelec thread. An earlier code-only baseline also
timed out a Fuchsreiter reply.
These are not clean passes of the literal every-reply-within-60-seconds acceptance rule. The runner
now polls slow POSTs after 3 seconds, waits for rivals no longer than 45 seconds after its own reply,
and refreshes on refused accepts. The remaining idle-bidder timing policy conflict is explicit.
Hosted records lack per-email delivery timestamps, so absence of timeout records is evidence, not a
proof of an exact maximum end-to-end reply latency.

[DESIGN_NOTES.md](DESIGN_NOTES.md) collects precedence and judgement calls. Important deviations:
whole-cent quantization prevents literal EUR 1 equal-cost precision on large lots; opening-price-only
cost estimates are exempted from the inherited full-cost anchor/floor; and voluntarily idling an RFQ
bidder can conflict with literal universal reply timing. The demanded-index/revealed-price policy
also needs further performance tuning. None is silently counted as full requirement compliance.

No final-wave sessions were started, no unrelated user files were removed, and no commit was made.
The completed artifacts are ready for review, but score/timing acceptance is not yet fully achieved.
   anchor (R4, R13.12) and the floor (R2.1, R6.5).
5. The must-have filter every sheet and every accept passes through.
6. The clock: `round_limit` and, in the final, `seconds_left`.

## Evidence

From `knowledge/sessions.jsonl` on `feature/team-agent` (practice sessions, 10 Oct 2026).

### Where BuyerAgent was better

| Case | Type / goal | BuyerAgent | DualAgent (best of its runs) | Why BuyerAgent did as well or better |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P11 | quality / quality_first | **0.589** | 0.536 (3 runs) | Same price (EUR 46.00), quality cost EUR 5,724 vs 10,732; it kept going (7 e-mails) where DualAgent closed on "deadlock" after 5 |
| P18 | raw_material / leverage | **0.419** | 0.319 (3 runs) | Price EUR 260,700 vs 265,440; index clause EUR 1,173 vs 7,167; supplier conceded 9.8 % vs 8.2 % and answered "counter" in rounds 1-3 (DualAgent drew "hold" in rounds 2-3) |
| P01 | price_increase / stabilise | 0.931 | 0.941 | Within 0.01; no early-payment cost in its last two runs (DualAgent paid ~EUR 7.2k in 4 of 5 runs) |
| P04, P10 | - | 0.860, 0.655 | 0.860, 0.655 | Tie |

### Where DualAgent was better

| Case | Type / goal | DualAgent | BuyerAgent | Why DualAgent did better |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | price_increase / stabilise | **0.941** (best of all runs) | 0.931 | Data argument twice, rapport, an appreciative close; deal at 135.20 with the price from April 2027 |
| P02 | price_increase / stabilise | **0.385** | 0.211 | Kept the supplier healthy: relationship charge EUR 92 vs **124,110**, no index risk (BuyerAgent: EUR 17,158). BuyerAgent's lower price (351 vs 373) cost far more than it saved |
| P03 | renewal / stabilise | **0.919** (same in 3 runs) | 0.900 | Lower total spend (EUR 3,959,776 vs 3,967,013) in 4 e-mails instead of 6 |
| P05 | rfq / leverage | **0.444** | 0.372 | Talked to all three bidders (2-3 e-mails each), cited the cheaper rival, closed with the cheapest bidder (70240) - BuyerAgent wrote only once to it and closed with 70210 |
| P07 | bundling / routine | **0.721** | 0.702 | EUR 5.45 vs 5.48 after 5 e-mails, appreciative close |
| P08 | raw_material / leverage | **0.343** | 0.332 | EUR 5.61 vs 5.67 |

The runs were hours apart (BuyerAgent 18:4x, DualAgent 21:xx) and the shared `strategy.py` changed
in between, so part of a gap can come from the code version, not the agent design. Section 11 takes
only what is DualAgent's own.

### Where TeamAgent was better

TeamAgent's runs are not in `sessions.jsonl` (it logs through `team.evaluate`). These best runs
(`runs/best_runs.json`, `runs/best_replays/`) are its own by their e-mails: the signature
"Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing" from its prompt, its code-written planned-move text word for word
(P10), and run times matching its commits (v4-v9, 10 Oct 18:00-01:30). P07 is the least certain.

| Case | Type / goal | TeamAgent | DualAgent | BuyerAgent | What won it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

"""SpecAgent: the buyer agent of NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md. Code decides every number, the model
writes words only, and every model call has a code-written fallback.

  before the clock   dossiers and one profile call per supplier (section 1, `spec.dossier`)
  case open          section 0.7 (`spec.prep`): the case checked, C of every opening and C_alt,
                     coverage, levers, anchor, floor, must-have filter, the case clock
  every move         per thread: what its e-mail says (`spec.analyst`), our estimate of it (section 2),
                     the close rules (section 7, `spec.closing`), else the next offer - the target C
                     from section 5 (`spec.concession`), the sheets from MESO's steps while heavy terms
                     are open (`spec.steps`) and section 6's sheets after (`spec.sheets`), guarded -
                     and an e-mail around them (`spec.email`) in one tactic's words (`spec.tactics`)
  runner             one worker per supplier thread (`spec.runner`)

    uv run arena play case:P01 --agent spec -v
"""

import json
import logging
import math
import os
import re
import threading
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from .. import claims as cl
from .. import writing
from ..cost import cost_breakdown, must_haves_ok
from ..docs import standard_terms
from ..play import latest, live_threads, moves_left
from ..spec import clock as clock_mod
from ..spec import closing, dossier, email, levers, prep, sheets, tactics
from ..spec import estimate as est_mod
from ..spec.analyst import GRACE_S, Analyst
from ..spec.concession import Plan
from ..spec.prose import prose_alternatives
from ..spec.steps import Steps, repeats
from ..spec.terms import COVERAGE, complete, key

log = logging.getLogger("arena")
WRITE_TIMEOUT_S = 35.0  # R10.1
SEND_MARGIN_S = 4.0  # compose and send after the model answers
VOLATILE_PCT = 15.0  # R13.11
PRESSURE_LEFT = 2  # R11.8
LOCK_RISK = 0.5  # R11.8
LOCK_TOL = 0.0005


@dataclass
class Thread:
    """What we keep per supplier thread."""

    plan: Plan = field(default_factory=Plan)
    steps: Steps = field(default_factory=Steps)
    analyst: Analyst | None = None
    last_sheets: list = field(default_factory=list)  # [(label, terms)] of our last message
    flags: set = field(default_factory=set)  # earlier, repair, restore, rival, weighted, volume
    sent_claims: list = field(default_factory=list)  # the arguments of our last message, in body order
    seen_replies: int = 0
    anchor_price: float | None = None


class SpecAgent:
    def __init__(self, complete=None, package=None, analyst_complete=None, prep_complete=None, log_dir=None):
        self.complete, self.package = complete, package
        self.analyst_complete = analyst_complete if analyst_complete is not None else complete
        self.prep_complete = prep_complete if prep_complete is not None else complete
        self.log_dir = Path(log_dir or os.environ.get("SPEC_LOG_DIR", "runs/spec-logs"))
        self.case_id, self.primed = None, None
        self.reply_at, self.inflight = {}, {}  # set by the runner
        self.lock = threading.RLock()
        self.dossiers, self.profiles, self.t = {}, {}, {}
        self.records, self._volatile = [], {}
        self.pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8, thread_name_prefix="spec")

    # --- the runner's entry -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def run_case(self, table, case_id, deadline=None):
        from ..spec.runner import play_case

        return play_case(table, case_id, self, deadline)

    # --- before the clock (section 1) ---------------------------------------------------------------
    def prime(self, case, timeout=None):
        """Dossiers and profiles before the session opens. In the final the profile budget leaves room
        for the 420 s case clock inside the wave's cap."""
        c, _ = prep.normalise(case)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        self.dossiers = {sid: dossier.gather(self.package, c, sid) for sid in c["suppliers"]}
        if timeout is None:
            timeout = dossier.PROFILE_TIMEOUT_S
            if isinstance(c.get("seconds_left"), int | float):
                timeout = min(timeout, max(0.0, c["seconds_left"] - clock_mod.FORCE_CLOSE_AT - 30))
        self.profiles = dossier.profiles(c, self.package, self.dossiers, self.prep_complete, timeout)
        self.primed = c["case_id"]
        log.info("%s primed in %.1fs (profiles: %s)", c["case_id"], time.monotonic() - t0,
                 {s: p.get("source") for s, p in self.profiles.items()})  # fmt: skip

    # --- case open (section 0.7) ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    def prepare(self, case, threads=None, seconds_left=None):
        if self.primed != case.get("case_id"):  # resumed, or no case file before the session: no model
            self.prime(case, timeout=0)
        cash = {sid: p.get("cash_short", False) for sid, p in self.profiles.items()}
        self.case = case  # hidden-case facts must be available to volatile() during preparation
        self._volatile.clear()
        self.prep = prep.prepare(case, threads, self.package, self.volatile, seconds_left, cash)
        self.case, self.case_id = self.prep.case, case.get("case_id")
        self.clock = self.prep.clock.open()
        self.ledger, self.results = cl.Ledger(), {}
        self.t = {}
        for sid in self.case["suppliers"]:
            self.t[sid] = Thread(
                analyst=Analyst(
                    self.case,
                    sid,
                    self.package,
                    self.analyst_complete,
                    self.pool,
                    cost_fn=lambda terms, std: est_mod.plain_cost(self.case, terms, std),
                )
            )
        log.info("%s", prep.summary(self.prep))
        self.record("prepare", summary=prep.summary(self.prep), warnings=self.prep.warnings)

    def volatile(self, series):
        """R13.11: the series moved more than VOLATILE_PCT in its last 12 months."""
        if series not in self._volatile:
            got = cl.index_change(self.package, getattr(self, "case", {}) or {}, series)
            if got:
                a, b = self.fact(got[1]), self.fact(got[2])
                change = (b["value"] / a["value"] - 1) * 100
                # Claim sentences round to a tenth; a risk threshold must not round 15.04% away.
                self._volatile[series] = abs(change) > VOLATILE_PCT + 1e-9
            else:
                self._volatile[series] = False
        return self._volatile[series]

    # --- clock hooks for the runner -----------------------------------------------------------------
    def sent(self, sid):
        if hasattr(self, "clock"):
            self.clock.sent(sid)

    def replied(self, sid):
        if hasattr(self, "clock"):
            self.clock.replied(sid)

    # --- the state of a thread ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _std(self, events):
        try:
            return standard_terms(events)
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("standard terms unreadable: %s", e)
            return {}

    def state(self, threads, sid):
        """Everything code needs about one thread now: rows, estimate, context, target, view."""
        case, events, th = self.case, threads[sid], self.t[sid]
        std = self._std(events)
        th.analyst.observe(events)
        intel = th.analyst.snapshot()
        replies = [m for m in events if m.get("from") != "buyer"]
        self._feedback(sid, events, len(replies))
        mine = " ".join(str(m.get("body") or "") for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer").lower()
        echo = bool(re.search(r"faster payment|cash ?flow|liquidit", mine))
        cash = self.profiles.get(sid, {}).get("cash_short", False) or (intel.cash_ask and not echo)  # R11.7, R12.19
        extra = [prose_alternatives(case, m) if m.get("from") != "buyer" else [] for m in events]
        slopes = levers.revealed_slopes(case, events, extra)
        seen = [r.terms["unit_price"] for s in threads for r in self._price_rows(threads, s)]
        # the market is judged on the opening quotes only: a later concession under the should-cost must
        # not drop the margin charge mid-case (P02: 373 against a should-cost of 374.95)
        market = [p for s in threads if (p := prep.opening_terms(threads[s]).get("unit_price"))]
        est = est_mod.estimate(case, self.package, events, prep.opening_terms(events), cash,
                               levers.revealed_rate(slopes), min(market, default=None))  # fmt: skip
        c_alt = self.prep.c_alt
        rows = []
        for n, m in enumerate(replies):
            for j, ts in enumerate(m.get("term_sheets") or []):
                terms = ts.get("terms") or {}
                if not ts.get("term_sheet_id") or terms.get("unit_price") is None:
                    continue
                c = est_mod.cost(case, terms, std, est)
                plain = est_mod.plain_cost(case, terms, std)
                valid = must_haves_ok(case, terms, std) and plain < c_alt and c < c_alt
                try:
                    bd = cost_breakdown(case, terms, std)
                    unc = bd["uncovered_need"] + bd["fallback_risk"]
                except Exception:
                    unc = 0.0
                rows.append(closing.Row(ts["term_sheet_id"], terms, c, valid, n == len(replies) - 1, j == 0, n, unc))
        latest_rows = [r for r in rows if r.latest]
        best = min(latest_rows, key=lambda r: (not r.valid, r.c)) if latest_rows else None
        their = complete(case, best.terms if best else {"unit_price": None}, std)
        ctx = sheets.Ctx(case, std, est, their, self.prep.row, self.volatile)
        out = {"sid": sid, "events": events, "std": std, "intel": intel, "est": est, "rows": rows, "best": best,
               "ctx": ctx, "slopes": slopes, "alternatives": extra[-1] if extra else [], "cash_short": cash,
               "status": latest(events).get("status") if replies else None, "left": moves_left(case, events),
               "sent": sum(m.get("from") == "buyer" and not m.get("undelivered") for m in events)}  # fmt: skip
        if best is None or not their.get("unit_price"):
            out.update(target=None, info={}, base=None, locked={}, c_ref=math.inf, only_price=False)
            return out
        locked = th.steps.locked(ctx, events)
        # R13.5: actual supplier-priced alternatives supersede an earlier blind menu pick.
        locked.update(th.steps.revealed(ctx, latest(events), out["alternatives"]))
        out["locked"] = locked
        # the anchor: fixed per thread (R4.4); in an RFQ every bidder is anchored to the lowest price on the
        # table and the anchor may only fall (R4.3, R12.6)
        rfq = len(self.case["suppliers"]) > 1
        seen = seen or [ctx.their_price]
        anchor_c = None
        if th.anchor_price is None or rfq:
            base0 = {k: v for k, v in sheets.repair(case, their, std).items() if k != "unit_price"}
            p0 = prep.anchor_price(case, ctx, ctx.their_price, min(seen + [ctx.their_price]), base0)
            combo = sheets.reference_combo(ctx, sheets.cover(ctx, base0, p0), ctx.their_price)
            p = prep.anchor_price(case, ctx, ctx.their_price, min(seen + [ctx.their_price]), combo)
            th.anchor_price = p if th.anchor_price is None else min(th.anchor_price, p)
            anchor_c = ctx.c({**combo, "unit_price": th.anchor_price})
        base = sheets.structure(ctx, th.anchor_price)
        base.update({f: v for f, v in locked.items() if f in base})
        ctx.locked = dict(locked)
        out["base"] = base
        c_ref = min(ctx.c({**base, "unit_price": ctx.their_price}), best.c)
        th.plan.observe(c_ref, len(replies))
        if anchor_c is not None and (th.plan.anchor is None or rfq):
            th.plan.set_anchor(min(anchor_c, c_ref), rfq)
        rival = [o.c for s, o in ((s, self._best_valid(threads, s)) for s in live_threads(threads) if s != sid) if o]
        target, info = th.plan.next_target(c_ref, self.prep.horizon, out["left"], c_alt, min(rival, default=None), rfq)
        out.update(target=target, info=info, c_ref=c_ref, rival_best=min(rival, default=None),
                   only_price=th.steps.next_field(ctx, base, locked) is None)  # fmt: skip
        return out

    def _price_rows(self, threads, sid):
        out = []
        for m in threads[sid]:
            if m.get("from") == "buyer":
                continue
            for ts in m.get("term_sheets") or []:
                if (ts.get("terms") or {}).get("unit_price"):
                    out.append(closing.Row(ts.get("term_sheet_id") or "", ts["terms"], 0.0, True, False))
        return out

    def _best_valid(self, threads, sid):
        std = self._std(threads[sid])
        best = None
        msg = latest(threads[sid]) if any(m.get("from") != "buyer" for m in threads[sid]) else {}
        for ts in msg.get("term_sheets") or []:
            terms = ts.get("terms") or {}
            if not terms.get("unit_price") or not must_haves_ok(self.case, terms, std):
                continue
            c = est_mod.plain_cost(self.case, terms, std)
            if c < self.prep.c_alt and (best is None or c < best.c):
                best = closing.Row(ts.get("term_sheet_id"), terms, c, True, True)
        return best

    def rival(self, threads, sid, st):
        """The rival offer to cite (R12.14): the cheapest valid rival sheet that costs us less than this
        bidder's; else the lowest rival price on the table under this bidder's price - the arena checks
        only the price (P05's 0.781 run cited offer:70240-0, whose lead time broke our must-have)."""
        mine = st["best"]
        if mine is None:
            return None
        valid = [b for s in live_threads(threads) if s != sid and (b := self._best_valid(threads, s)) and b.id]
        valid = [b for b in valid if b.c < mine.c]
        if valid:
            return min(valid, key=lambda b: b.c)
        prices = []
        for s in live_threads(threads):
            if s == sid or not any(m.get("from") != "buyer" for m in threads[s]):
                continue
            for ts in latest(threads[s]).get("term_sheets") or []:
                p = (ts.get("terms") or {}).get("unit_price")
                if ts.get("term_sheet_id") and p and p < mine.terms.get("unit_price", 0):
                    prices.append(closing.Row(ts["term_sheet_id"], ts["terms"], p, False, True))
        return min(prices, key=lambda r: r.c) if prices else None

    def _feedback(self, sid, events, n_replies):
        """R10.3: every argument's claim result, fed into the next round."""
        th = self.t[sid]
        if n_replies <= th.seen_replies:
            return
        th.seen_replies = n_replies
        for r in latest(events).get("claim_results") or []:
            i = r.get("index")
            if i is not None and i < len(th.sent_claims):
                self.results[th.sent_claims[i].key] = r.get("result")
                if r.get("result") == "contradicted":
                    log.warning("%s: argument %s was contradicted", sid, th.sent_claims[i].key)

    def view(self, st):
        th = self.t[st["sid"]]
        cs = []
        for n in sorted({r.reply for r in st["rows"]}):
            rs = [r.c for r in st["rows"] if r.reply == n]
            cs.append(min(rs))
        step_share = (cs[-2] - cs[-1]) / cs[-2] if len(cs) > 1 and cs[-2] else 0.0
        return closing.View(
            sid=st["sid"], status=st["status"], left=st["left"], sent=st["sent"], rows=st["rows"],
            target=st.get("target"), last_target=th.plan.targets[-1] if th.plan.targets else None,
            moving=bool((st.get("info") or {}).get("still_moving")), only_price=bool(st.get("only_price")),
            planned_over=len(th.plan.targets) >= self.prep.horizon + 2, close_gap=self.prep.row["close_gap"],
            replies_c=cs, earlier_used="earlier" in th.flags, repair_used="repair" in th.flags,
            restore_used="restore" in th.flags, last_step_share=step_share,
        )  # fmt: skip

    def views(self, threads):
        states = {s: self.state(threads, s) for s in live_threads(threads)}
        return states, {s: self.view(st) for s, st in states.items()}

    # --- the move ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def decide(self, case, threads, sid=None, use_model=True):
        if case.get("case_id") != self.case_id:
            self.prepare(case, threads)
        live = live_threads(threads)
        if sid is None:  # the kit's sequential loop: the thread whose offer costs least
            sid = min(live, key=lambda s: self.standing_cost(case, threads, s))
        if sid not in live:
            return {"supplier_id": sid, "idle": True}
        th = self.t[sid]
        th.analyst.observe(threads[sid])
        first_rfq = len(self.case["suppliers"]) > 1 and not any(m.get("from") == "buyer" for m in threads[sid])
        terminal = latest(threads[sid]).get("status") in ("agreed", "final_offer")
        if use_model and self.analyst_complete is not None and not first_rfq and not terminal:
            # R11.3: a short grace; R12.14 first RFQ / R13.16 terminal offers go straight to code.
            since = time.monotonic() - self.reply_at.get(sid, time.monotonic())
            th.analyst.wait(min(GRACE_S, max(0.0, clock_mod.MODEL_WINDOW_S - since - 25)))
        with self.lock:
            states, views = self.views(threads)
            st = states[sid]
            close = closing.decide(views, sid, must_close=self.clock.must_close())
            if close is None and not self.clock.can_counter():
                close = self.late(states, views, sid)
            if close is not None:
                d = self.realise(close, states, threads, sid)
                if d is not None:
                    self.record("close", sid=sid, kind=close.kind, reason=close.reason, sheet=close.sheet_id,
                                elapsed=round(self.clock.elapsed(), 1))  # fmt: skip
                    return d
            if st.get("target") is None:  # no price on the table: ask for one
                return self.plain_message(threads, sid, [], "Could you please send us your offer with a unit price?")
            move = self.plan_move(states, views, threads, sid)
            if move is None or "sheets" not in move:  # a close, an offer-back or nothing left to send
                return move or {"supplier_id": sid, "idle": True}
        return self.write(states, threads, sid, move, use_model)

    def late(self, states, views, sid):
        """R11.16, after NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT: lock in a better prose offer if a round still fits; repeat our
        last offer only when nothing on the table is acceptable yet; otherwise close by R7."""
        fits = self.clock.round_fits()
        st, th = states[sid], self.t[sid]
        lock = self.lock_in(st)
        best_rows = [r for v in views.values() for r in v.rows if r.valid]
        if fits and lock and (not best_rows or lock[1] < min(r.c for r in best_rows) - 0.01) and "lock" not in th.flags:
            return closing.Close("lock_in", "late: lock in its prose offer", sid, terms=lock[0])
        if fits and not closing.ladder(views) and th.last_sheets and st["left"] > 1:
            return closing.Close("repeat", "late: nothing acceptable yet - our last offer again", sid)
        return closing.accept(views, "late: no new counter-offers") or closing.Close("idle", "late, nothing yet", sid)

    def lock_in(self, st):
        """R11.8: the supplier's best offer stated only in prose, if it keeps the must-haves, beats the
        alternative and is cheaper than its standing sheet: (terms, C) or None."""
        if st.get("best") is None:
            return None
        ctx, best = st["ctx"], None
        for po in st["intel"].prose_offers:
            if po.get("in_sheet"):
                continue
            t = complete(self.case, po["terms"], st["std"])
            if not t.get("unit_price") or not ctx.ok(t):
                continue
            c = ctx.c(t)
            if c < st["best"].c - 0.01 and est_mod.plain_cost(self.case, t, st["std"]) < self.prep.c_alt:
                if best is None or c < best[1]:
                    best = (t, c)
        return best

    def realise(self, close, states, threads, sid):
        """A close rule as a decision: accept, walk, idle, or a one-off message written by code."""
        th = self.t.get(close.sid or sid)
        if close.kind == "accept":
            return {"supplier_id": close.sid, "reason": close.reason, "candidates": close.candidates,
                    "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": close.sheet_id}}}  # fmt: skip
        if close.kind == "walk":
            return {"supplier_id": close.sid or sid, "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
        if close.kind == "idle":
            return {"supplier_id": sid, "idle": True}
        st = states[close.sid or sid]
        if close.kind == "offer_back":  # R12.13
            th.flags.add("earlier")
            t = complete(self.case, close.terms, st["std"])
            text = (
                f"Thank you. We have reviewed everything again and are ready to sign on your own earlier offer "
                f"{close.sheet_id} - the attached term sheet repeats exactly those terms. Can you confirm?"
            )
            return self.plain_message(threads, close.sid, [("their earlier offer", t)], text)
        if close.kind in ("repair", "restore"):  # R12.12 / R11.17: its price, must-haves kept, full need covered
            th.flags.add(close.kind)
            terms = close.terms or (st["best"].terms if st.get("best") else latest(st["events"]).get("term_sheets",
                                    [{}])[0].get("terms", {}))  # fmt: skip
            t = complete(self.case, sheets.repair(self.case, terms, st["std"]), st["std"])

                continue

            out[f] = min(enough) if enough else max(opts)

def run_case(self, table, case_id, deadline=None):
        from ..spec.runner import play_case

        return play_case(table, case_id, self, deadline)

    # --- before the clock (section 1) ---------------------------------------------------------------
    def prime(self, case, timeout=None):
        """Dossiers and profiles before the session opens. In the final the profile budget leaves room
        for the 420 s case clock inside the wave's cap."""
        c, _ = prep.normalise(case)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        self.dossiers = {sid: dossier.gather(self.package, c, sid) for sid in c["suppliers"]}
        if timeout is None:
            timeout = dossier.PROFILE_TIMEOUT_S
            if isinstance(c.get("seconds_left"), int | float):
                timeout = min(timeout, max(0.0, c["seconds_left"] - clock_mod.FORCE_CLOSE_AT - 30))
        self.profiles = dossier.profiles(c, self.package, self.dossiers, self.prep_complete, timeout)
        self.primed = c["case_id"]
        log.info("%s primed in %.1fs (profiles: %s)", c["case_id"], time.monotonic() - t0,
                 {s: p.get("source") for s, p in self.profiles.items()})  # fmt: skip

    # --- case open (section 0.7) ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    def prepare(self, case, threads=None, seconds_left=None):
        if self.primed != case.get("case_id"):  # resumed, or no case file before the session: no model
            self.prime(case, timeout=0)
        cash = {sid: p.get("cash_short", False) for sid, p in self.profiles.items()}
        self.case = case  # hidden-case facts must be available to volatile() during preparation
        self._volatile.clear()
        self.prep = prep.prepare(case, threads, self.package, self.volatile, seconds_left, cash)
        self.case, self.case_id = self.prep.case, case.get("case_id")
        self.clock = self.prep.clock.open()
        self.ledger, self.results = cl.Ledger(), {}
        self.t = {}
        for sid in self.case["suppliers"]:
            self.t[sid] = Thread(
                analyst=Analyst(
                    self.case,
                    sid,

content.text:
It already is a combined agent. **`SpecAgent`** (`--agent spec`) merges the four earlier agents into one: BuyerAgent, DualAgent, TeamAgent and MESO. It isn't four agents running side by side. The best parts of each were rebuilt as modules in `arena_kit/spec/`, following [NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md](NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md).

## Where each part comes from

| Source agent | What SpecAgent takes from it | Requirements sections |
|---|---|---|
| **BuyerAgent** | Preparation, the estimate of the supplier's costs, anchor, concessions, term sheets, close rules, e-mail structure | §1–10 |
| **DualAgent** | A background analyst that reads each supplier e-mail, offers stated only in prose, wording tactics, the case clock | §11 |
| **TeamAgent** | The first message carries the deal (full coverage), levers priced in euros, RFQ rival citation, the accept ladder, one worker per supplier thread | §12 |
| **MESO** (`agents/llm.py`) | Heavy terms settled one at a time with equal-cost choices (payment, index, ppm), fact-checked data arguments, e-mails built by code | §13 |

Where the rules from different agents overlap, the outcome is recorded in [DESIGN_NOTES.md](DESIGN_NOTES.md). For example, the anchor uses the deeper cut, and a valid final offer is accepted at once.

## The main rule

**Code decides every number. The model only writes words**, and every model call has a deadline and a code fallback. Prices, term sheets, accept and walk decisions, claims and deadlines all come from code. The model profiles suppliers, pulls facts out of their e-mails and writes the text around the offer. With `SPEC_LLM=0`, or no credentials, the agent runs fully on code.

## How a case runs

```
arena play case:P01 --agent spec
        │
cli.agent_factory ──► agents/spec.make()   (3 model clients: writer, analyst, profiler)
        │
spec/runner.play_case
  1. BEFORE THE CLOCK  agent.prime()    dossier.py: data per supplier + one profile call each
  2. OPEN SESSION      agent.prepare()  prep.py: check the case, cost of every opening quote,
                                        cost of the fallback, coverage, levers, anchor, floor,
                                        must-have filter, start clock.py
  3. ONE WORKER PER SUPPLIER THREAD (parallel, each has its own 60 s reply clock)
        loop: agent.decide(sid)
          ├─ analyst.py     what did their e-mail say? (background, short wait)
          ├─ estimate.py    their full cost, our total-cost view of each sheet
          ├─ closing.py     accept / walk / accept ladder?  ── yes ─► accept (RFQ: wait ≤45 s for rivals)
          ├─ concession.py  next target cost (curve + reciprocity + deadlock breaker)
          ├─ steps.py       a heavy term still open? → a one-term equal-cost menu (MESO)
          │  sheets.py      otherwise → price-round sheets (reference/give/decoy), guarded
          └─ email.py + tactics.py + claims.py   code-built options + checked claims,
                                                 model writes the text, lint removes leaks
  4. CLOCK GUARDS      no new counter after 360 s, force close by 420 s
```

The main files:
- **Entry point:** [agents/spec.py](arena_kit/agents/spec.py). Most of the logic sits in `decide()` at line 311, and `plan_move()` at line 432 builds the next offer.
- **Concurrency, retries, accept timing:** [spec/runner.py](arena_kit/spec/runner.py).
- **Code shared with MESO:** `claims.py`, `writing.py`, `play.py` and `cost.py` in `arena_kit/`.

## Running it

```bash
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent spec -v
```
```bash
uv run arena run --set practice --agent spec
```
```bash
uv run python -m arena_kit.spec.evaluate --sim
```

The evaluator saves full threads, decision logs and a score table to a new folder under `runs/`. `--set sandbox` plays D01 and D02 instead of the local simulator cases.

## Where it stands

According to [FINAL_REPORT.md](FINAL_REPORT.md):
- 204 tests passed, 1 skipped.
- All 10 practice cases ended in a deal, all closed before 420 s, and there were no contradicted claims.
- Only P02, P04 and P11 reach their score targets. The model sweep averaged 61.1 against a target of 71.6; the code-only sweep averaged 65.3.
- The furthest behind are P01, P05, P08 and P18, mostly on anchor, payment and index-band calibration.
- One supplier thread the agent deliberately stopped answering (in P05) still hit a reply timeout.

The repo still has three selectable agents: `naive`, `llm` (MESO) and `spec`. If by "combined" you meant folding those into one, so `spec` is the only agent with no separate MESO class, that's a cleanup I can do. Just confirm.

content.text:
The difference is whether the language model is switched on. In both sweeps, code sets every price, term sheet and accept decision.

## What changes between them

| | Model sweep | Code-only sweep |
|---|---|---|
| How it's started | `evaluate` → `make(package)` | `evaluate --no-model` → `SpecAgent(package=...)` with no model |
| Supplier profiles before the clock | One model call per supplier: whether they seem short of cash, which arguments to lead with, questions to ask | None |
| Reading supplier replies | Model analyst in the background (cash requests, relationship style, how far they are from their costs), plus code parsing | Code parsing only (offers in prose, revealed prices) |
| E-mail text | Model writes the text around the code-built options and checked claims; lint removes anything risky | Fixed code templates |
| Code version | Ran **before** the last lead-time and volatility fixes | Final code |

## Why the scores still differ when code sets the numbers

1. **Some model output feeds into the decisions.** If a supplier looks short of cash ([agents/spec.py:167](arena_kit/agents/spec.py:167)), that changes the estimated cost of money and so how payment terms are valued. The profile's argument ranking also changes which data claims go into the e-mail.
2. **The suppliers react to wording.** The arena's suppliers are themselves AI-simulated, so different text gets different replies. Those replies then move every number that follows.
3. **The code versions differ.** P05 shows this most: the lead-time fix came after the model sweep. A model retest with the fix scored 0.573, against 0.522 in the sweep.

## Results

- **Identical** in both: P02, P03, P04, P11.
- **Code-only higher**: P01 (0.83 vs 0.63), P05, P07, P08, P10.
- **Model higher**: P18 only (0.32 vs 0.27).
- **Mean**: 65.3 code-only vs 61.1 with the model.

## Timing

Most code-only games closed in about 5 seconds; the model games took 35–322 seconds. Code-only sends the same text every time, and the report puts the speed down to fast cached supplier responses. So code-only timing says nothing about real latency, and it may be replaying familiar supplier behaviour.

## What this means

As measured, the model is not helping yet, and it hurt P01 badly. But this is one run each, on different code versions, so the comparison isn't clean. A fair test would be a fresh model sweep on the final code. That uses 10 of your practice sessions, so I'd only start it with your go-ahead.

        state = Sim(load_cases(), package.facts)
        server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(state), log_level="error"))

            cases = [c for c in cases if c["case_id"] in ids]
            if {c["case_id"] for c in cases} != ids:
                raise ValueError("one or more requested cases are unavailable")
        if args.capture_session:
            if len(cases) != 1:
                raise ValueError("capture requires exactly one case")
            case = cases[0]
            state = client.session(args.capture_session)
            if state.get("case_id") != case["case_id"] or state.get("status") != "ended":
                raise ValueError("capture session must be ended and match the requested case")
            threads = {sid: client.thread(args.capture_session, sid) for sid in case["suppliers"]}
            args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
            record = {"case_id": case["case_id"], "session_id": args.capture_session, "session": state,
                      "result": state.get("result"), "threads": threads,
                      "audit": audit(threads)}
            write_json(args.out / f"{case['case_id'].split(':')[-1]}.json", record)
        else:
            evaluate(client, cases, args.out, package, args.parallel, args.no_model)
    finally:
        if server:
            server.should_exit = True


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
