content.text:
The new model run averaged **60.1**, about the same as the previous model run (61.1). The total is dragged down by one case: **P02 ended with no deal and scored 0**. Leaving P02 out, the other nine average 66.7. Separately, **P05 scored 0.824**, which beats its 0.781 target and your team's best ever on that case (0.7805).

I didn't need to change the model: `.env` already had `gpt-6-astra`, the same model as before. This run used the final, pushed code.

| Case | Target | Previous model run | Code-only run | **New model run** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P01 | 0.941 | 0.631 | 0.828 | 0.631 |
| P02 | 0.507 | 0.507 | 0.507 | **0.000 (no deal)** |
| P03 | 0.919 | 0.864 | 0.864 | 0.843 |
| P04 | 0.860 | 0.860 | 0.860 | 0.860 ✓ |
| P05 | 0.781 | 0.522 | 0.676 | **0.824 ✓** (EUR 28.00) |
| P07 | 0.773 | 0.715 | 0.753 | 0.728 |
| P08 | 0.549 | 0.332 | 0.394 | 0.427 |
| P10 | 0.671 | 0.647 | 0.663 | 0.647 |
| P11 | 0.710 | 0.710 | 0.710 | 0.710 ✓ |
| P18 | 0.453 | 0.319 | 0.270 | 0.336 |
| **Mean** | **71.6** | **61.1** | **65.3** | **60.1** |

**Timing and claims:** no reply timeouts (this time including the idle P05 bidder), no contradicted claims, no e-mail missing the company name. Every case closed by 283 seconds from open, well inside 420.

**What went wrong in P02:** our offers and the supplier's were identical to the previous run, to the cent, through four rounds. The supplier came down to EUR 371.88 and said the copper cost pressure "limits our flexibility". We kept answering with small steps up (EUR 352 → 355). Last time the supplier then made a final offer at 371.88 and we accepted it for 0.507. This time it walked away. So the agent keeps countering a supplier that is barely moving, and P02 only works when the supplier happens to make a final offer. This is a real weak spot, not just a bad draw.

**Possible fix:** accept the best valid offer on the table when the supplier is moving less than about 0.5% a round and says it has little room left. The catch: [DESIGN_NOTES.md](DESIGN_NOTES.md) deliberately says walk risk is never a close rule on its own, and this would loosen that. I'd need your go-ahead to change it.

The results are saved in `runs/spec-practice-astra-final/`, uncommitted. They used 10 of your 433 practice sessions. Should I make the P02 change, commit and push these results, or both?

content.text:
Yes, the outcome changed, even with nothing changed. The repeat averaged **62.2**, against 60.1 last time. Six of the ten cases came out different, and the agent didn't decide the swings: the suppliers did.

| Case | Target | Run 1 | **Run 2** | What changed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P01 | 0.941 | 0.631 | 0.667 | EUR 135.70 → 135.40 |
| P02 | 0.507 | **0.000** (walked) | **0.476** | This time the supplier made a final offer (EUR 372.15) and we accepted it |
| P03 | 0.919 | 0.843 | 0.864 | EUR 430.88 → 430.09 |
| P04 | 0.860 | 0.860 | 0.860 | Identical |
| P05 | 0.781 | **0.824** | **0.625** | The EUR 28.00 bidder walked this time; we closed with another bidder at EUR 30.00 |
| P07 | 0.773 | 0.728 | 0.740 | EUR 5.44 → 5.42 |
| P08 | 0.549 | 0.427 | 0.427 | Identical |
| P10 | 0.671 | 0.647 | 0.647 | Identical |
| P11 | 0.710 | 0.710 | 0.626 | Supplier stopped at EUR 46.00 instead of 45.50 |
| P18 | 0.453 | 0.336 | 0.286 | Same EUR 5.70, but 30-day payment instead of 90 |
| **Mean** | **71.6** | **60.1** | **62.2** | |

**The big swings in P02 and P05 come from the same weak spot, from opposite sides.** In both cases a supplier reached a good price while still open (EUR 371.88 in P02, EUR 28.00 in P05), and we sent one more counter. The supplier then either made a final offer at that price, which we accepted, or walked away. Which one happens looks like a coin flip on the supplier's side:
- **P02:** walked in run 1; made a final offer in run 2 and in the earlier model run.
- **P05:** made a final offer at EUR 28.00 in run 1, which was your best-ever score on that case; walked in run 2.

One counter too many can cost 0.2–0.5 of a case's score.

**Stable cases:** P04, P08 and P10 came out identical both times, and P01, P03 and P07 moved by a few cents. These don't depend on luck; their gaps to target are about strategy (anchor, payment terms, index clause).

**One timeout:** an uncompetitive P05 bidder that the agent deliberately stopped answering timed out again. There were no contradicted claims, and every case closed by 220 seconds.

**What I'd suggest:** when a supplier offers a price that is valid, beats the alternative and is near our estimate of its cost, and it is moving less than about 0.5% a round or says it has little room left, accept that open offer instead of countering again. This would have locked in P02 at 0.507 and P05 at 0.824 in both runs. It loosens the rule in [DESIGN_NOTES.md](DESIGN_NOTES.md) that walk risk alone never triggers a close, so it's your call.

Run 2's results are in `runs/spec-practice-astra-repeat/`, uncommitted like run 1's. The two runs used 20 practice sessions, leaving 413. Should I implement that accept rule?
